rows.quote: To ensure homogeneity in proteome analysis, we extracted proteome data of randomly selected baseline participants from protein batches 0–6, which are highly representative of the UK Biobank overall26.
rows.reference_quote: Sun, B. B. et al. Plasma proteomic associations with genetics and health in the UK biobank. Nature 622 (7982), 329–338 (2023).
rows.coder_note: Step 2, rules E and C5: the sentence attributes the proteome data to reference 26 (Sun 2023, DOI 10.1038/s41586-023-06592-6, the source of four pqtl rows) and gives the subcohort attribute 'randomly selected baseline participants from protein batches 0–6', which matches exactly one of them. The final N of 30,272 unrelated Caucasian individuals is a post-QC, ancestry-subset N (rule H), not a conflict, so step 1 does not apply. The passages also describe the pQTLs as the authors' own sex-stratified GWAS of these individual-level data (project 44986, REGENIE), which rule C would take as absent at step 3; step 2 comes first in the order and was applied. No accession is given, so no case of rule C4 arises.
